warfarin::aspirin.description: Concurrent use increases bleeding risk significantly. Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation while warfarin impairs clotting factors.
warfarin::aspirin.recommendation: Avoid combination. If necessary, use lowest aspirin dose and monitor INR closely.

warfarin::ibuprofen.description: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may displace warfarin from protein binding, increasing bleeding risk.
warfarin::ibuprofen.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with warfarin. Use paracetamol for pain.

warfarin::ciprofloxacin.description: Fluoroquinolones inhibit CYP1A2, increasing warfarin plasma levels and INR.
warfarin::ciprofloxacin.recommendation: Monitor INR closely. Reduce warfarin dose if needed.

warfarin::metronidazole.description: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, substantially increasing warfarin levels and bleeding risk.
warfarin::metronidazole.recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%. Monitor INR every 2-3 days.

simvastatin::amiodarone.description: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, raising simvastatin levels and risk of myopathy.
simvastatin::amiodarone.recommendation: Limit simvastatin to 20mg/day. Consider switching to pravastatin.

clopidogrel::omeprazole.description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel conversion to active metabolite.
clopidogrel::omeprazole.recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead of omeprazole with clopidogrel.

ssri::maoi.description: Combination can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome: agitation, hyperthermia, tachycardia.

methotrexate::nsaids.description: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate causing toxic accumulation.
methotrexate::nsaids.recommendation: Avoid combination. Monitor FBC and renal function if unavoidable.

digoxin::amiodarone.description: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein, increasing digoxin plasma levels causing toxicity.
digoxin::amiodarone.recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 50%. Monitor digoxin levels and ECG.

lithium::thiazide.description: Thiazide diuretics reduce renal lithium clearance causing toxicity.
lithium::thiazide.recommendation: Avoid combination. Monitor lithium levels weekly if necessary.

metformin::alcohol.description: Alcohol potentiates lactic acidosis risk with metformin.
metformin::alcohol.recommendation: Advise patient to avoid binge drinking.

lisinopril::potassium.description: ACE inhibitors reduce potassium excretion; concurrent potassium supplements risk hyperkalaemia.
lisinopril::potassium.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium. Avoid potassium supplements unless documented deficiency.

lisinopril::spironolactone.description: Dual renin-angiotensin-aldosterone blockade increases hyperkalaemia risk.
lisinopril::spironolactone.recommendation: Monitor renal function and potassium monthly.

amlodipine::simvastatin.description: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.

clarithromycin::simvastatin.description: Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4, raising simvastatin levels.
clarithromycin::simvastatin.recommendation: Suspend simvastatin during clarithromycin course. Switch to pravastatin.

fluoxetine::tramadol.description: SSRIs inhibit CYP2D6 and risk of serotonin syndrome with tramadol.
fluoxetine::tramadol.recommendation: Monitor for serotonin syndrome. Consider alternative analgesic.

metformin::contrast.description: IV contrast can cause nephropathy, reducing metformin excretion and increasing lactic acidosis risk.
metformin::contrast.recommendation: Hold metformin 48h before and after IV contrast.

bisoprolol::verapamil.description: Both have negative chronotropic effects; combination risks complete heart block.

ciprofloxacin::antacids.description: Divalent cations chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing bioavailability by up to 90%.
ciprofloxacin::antacids.recommendation: Separate ciprofloxacin from antacids by at least 2 hours.

atorvastatin::grapefruit.description: Grapefruit juice inhibits CYP3A4, modestly increasing atorvastatin levels.
atorvastatin::grapefruit.recommendation: Advise patient to avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice.

aspirin::ibuprofen.description: Ibuprofen may interfere with aspirin platelet inhibition if taken concurrently.

amoxicillin::warfarin.description: Antibiotics alter gut flora reducing vitamin K synthesis, potentiating warfarin effect.
amoxicillin::warfarin.recommendation: Monitor INR during antibiotic course and 1 week after.

furosemide::gentamicin.description: Loop diuretics potentiate aminoglycoside ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
furosemide::gentamicin.recommendation: Monitor renal function and hearing. Use lowest effective doses.

phenytoin::carbamazepine.description: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing phenytoin levels; phenytoin induces carbamazepine metabolism.
phenytoin::carbamazepine.recommendation: Monitor drug levels closely. Dose adjustments likely needed.

rifampicin::oral_contraceptive.description: Rifampicin strongly induces CYP3A4, reducing contraceptive hormone levels and efficacy.
rifampicin::oral_contraceptive.recommendation: Use additional contraception during rifampicin therapy and for 4 weeks after.
